rules.reason: Personal pleasure priority does not establish hedonism as a theory of welfare.
Consequences mattering does not entail permissive instrumental harm.
Harm concern is not identical to relational moral reasoning.
Equality concern does not uniquely select a distributive doctrine.
Private divine belief does not determine religious public authority.
Atheism or theism does not determine physicalism.
Determinism and incompatibilism are different propositions.
Institution-dependent social entities do not determine methodological individualism or normative priority of groups.
Legal validity does not establish a duty to obey.
Epistemic fallibilism does not establish moral anti-realism.
Objective meaning does not require cosmic purpose.
Easy ontological methods do not decide which abstract objects exist.

gaps.reason: No generic Buddhism, Hinduism, Confucianism or Indigenous-worldview label may be derived from theism, authority or no-self answers. Dedicated primary scholarship and discriminating items are still required.
Consequence sensitivity and instrumental harm do not measure outcome-only rightness, aggregation, maximizing versus satisficing, and scope well enough to assert full utilitarianism.
The corpus recognizes constructivist objectivity and competing Kantian/Humean variants; the bank lacks sufficient direct procedural-grounding discriminants for a full comparison.
Socialism, liberalism, conservatism and religious traditions have internal variants; policy resemblance alone is insufficient for full-system identities.
Some legacy reverse-keyed items and forced choices contain insufficient-conditions or ambiguity problems; only explicit reviewed mappings enter comparisons.
All repository academic references are inventoried with access limits. This is not all academic literature, all datasets, or proof of universal cultural coverage.
